intelligence.essence: On a fast main, every observation is perishable. A headline announcing "Now on main (RUNG 1)" described a kit that lived only on a branch (SN-819); an hourly "nothing is broken" post was falsified four minutes later by a red tip (SN-823); regen evidence gathered inside a PR expired at the moment of merge, twice (SN-821); a merge executed on a PR record's stale base while two unreviewed pushes, landed before the scorecard was even written, had already falsified its base (SN-883). The family's law: **verify at the action instant, against the live ref, and carry nothing forward** — status claims are tip-anchored and timestamped or they are hope (SN-823), read and mutation must be adjacent (SN-883), and re-anchoring belongs at verify-time, not burned in advance against a tip that will move again (SN-889).
intelligence.human_view: Everything in this system moves — the code, the board, the record — and it moves fast. These notes are about what that does to truth: a fact about the system is only true *at a moment, at a version*. Saying "it's green" without saying *which* version and *when* is like saying "the shop is open" without a day or an hour. The discipline here is simply always naming the moment your fact belongs to — and re-checking at the moment you act, because the fifteen seconds between checking and acting is exactly where trouble rides in.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine a river. You take a picture of it and say "the river looks like this!" But the river keeps flowing — your picture is already old. Smart people write on the picture: "this is how it looked at 3 o'clock." And if they're about to jump in, they look at the river again *right before jumping*, not at the old picture.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's the milk rule, dear: check the date, and check it when you're about to pour, not when you bought it. These engineers learned that "it was fine a minute ago" is not a safety standard when a minute is all it takes for two strangers' changes to land inside your work. And they learned to write the date on everything — a claim without its date is just a rumor with confidence.
intelligence.ai_view: Anchor every status claim: "green at `<sha>` as of `<time>`," or don't make it (SN-823). 404-check live paths behind headlines — including your own tools' success output (SN-819). Split diagnostics into architecture (durable) and status (expires at write time), marking findings CONFIRMED/FIXED/STALE/UNKNOWN with source + SHA (SN-835). Run regen + `--check` post-merge at the exact merge tip (SN-821); replace two-dot diffs with rehearsed merges (SN-856). Immediately before any mutating call, `GET refs/heads/main` and name preconditions from that read; keep read and mutation adjacent (SN-883). On a superseded tip's failure, re-verify the final tip three ways and carry nothing forward (SN-879). Advance watermarks only over reconciled ID sets — fetch last page and last page − 1 (SN-853). Stage verification so re-anchoring happens at verify-time; post stale states openly (SN-889).
intelligence.what_it_means: Nine notes refine one ancestor law (SN-0493: a decision expires when the tip moves) into its working forms — for headlines, reports, diagnostics, regens, diffs, merge preconditions, failure observations, watermarks, and verification staging. The refinement that matters most is SN-883's: the expiry window is not the decision, it's the *gap between the last read and the mutation*, and on a busy main that gap is measured in seconds. Freshness is not a property a claim has; it's a property of the distance between the claim and the act.
whats_inside: Headlines and tool success messages are claims about the world; verify against the live path, annotate false claims, never erase them (SN-819).
Status claims are tip-anchored + timestamped or they are hope (SN-823); diagnostic status expires at write time while architecture survives, findings marked CONFIRMED/FIXED/STALE/UNKNOWN (SN-835).
Regen evidence gathered in-PR expires at merge; regen + `--check` run on a clean worktree at the exact merge tip (SN-821).
Two-dot diffs on a moved main manufacture phantom deletions; merge evidence is a rehearsed merge at the live tip (SN-856).
Base preconditions are re-read from the live ref immediately before the mutating call, parents named from that read — read and mutation adjacent (SN-883).
A failure anchored on a superseded tip is a race artifact; re-verify the final tip three ways, carry nothing forward (SN-879).
A watermark advances only over a reconciled ID set; unreconciled absence proves nothing (SN-853).
At high tip velocity, re-anchor at verify-time or take a merge-queue slot — never as repeated pre-verification work (SN-889).
